name: Spanish Classical

description.short: Plateresque and Churrigueresque — Spanish Renaissance and Baroque, in which classical structure carries an ornament of unmatched density.
description.long:
Spanish classicism concentrates rather than distributes. A plain wall of great expanse is punctuated by a single entry or retable of overwhelming elaboration — the strategy is one of contrast, not of even articulation, and it is the opposite of the French or English classical habit.

Carried to the Americas, this strategy suited a labour economy in which skilled carving was available for a single focal point and nothing else. The result — vast plain adobe or stone walls with one intensely worked doorway — became the defining move of Spanish Colonial Revival four centuries later.

defining_characteristics: Ornament concentrated at a single focal point against large plain surfaces
Classical structure carrying non-classical densities of decoration
The retable façade as the organizing device
Adaptation to labour economies where skilled carving is scarce
